good_to_know.explanation: The security deposit is one month's rent (€1,200), which is the maximum legally allowed.
good_to_know.title: Security Deposit Amount

missing_clauses.explanation: The lease doesn't provide contact information for reporting repairs, especially in emergencies. This means you might not know who to contact if something urgent breaks, like a burst pipe.
missing_clauses.recommendation: Ask your landlord to provide specific contact information for reporting repairs and emergencies. Get this in writing as an addendum to your lease.
missing_clauses.title: No Landlord Repair Contact

missing_clauses.explanation: The lease doesn't mention that the landlord is legally required to register the tenancy with the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB).
missing_clauses.recommendation: Ask your landlord to confirm in writing that the tenancy will be registered with the RTB. You can verify registration by requesting the RTB registration number or checking directly with the RTB.
missing_clauses.title: No RTB Registration Mention

missing_clauses.explanation: The lease doesn't explicitly guarantee your right to quiet and peaceful enjoyment of the property without unreasonable interference from the landlord.
missing_clauses.recommendation: Request that your landlord add a clause acknowledging your right to quiet and peaceful enjoyment. Even if not explicitly stated, this right is protected by law under the Residential Tenancies Act.
missing_clauses.title: No Peaceful Occupation Clause

missing_clauses.explanation: The lease doesn't specify how and when the rent may be reviewed or increased. This is important to know, as there are rules about how often and by how much rent can be increased.
missing_clauses.recommendation: Ask your landlord to include clear terms about rent reviews, including the legally required 90-day notice period and 12-month minimum between increases. Note that these protections apply even if not explicitly stated in your lease.
missing_clauses.title: No Rent Review Clause

missing_clauses.explanation: The lease doesn't mention an inventory or condition report. This report documents the state of the property and its contents at the start of your tenancy, which is important for avoiding disputes about damage when you move out.
missing_clauses.recommendation: Request a detailed inventory and condition report before moving in. Take photos of the property condition and any existing damage. Have the landlord sign and date this report to avoid future disputes about the property's original condition.
missing_clauses.title: No Inventory and Condition Report
